subject: [hw] R1 -> IP: vcodecds V-interface calls match n2ap_venc.h; the DMA PA gap is a V40/V41 feature, not a misuse
body:
I checked the V-interface use in daemon/vcodecd.c (not a full track P review; R2 owns that):
  n2ap_venc_open(&enc, g.vcu, g.vhw, fourcc, timeout) matches the header (struct n2ap_venc **, struct n2vcu *, const struct n2vc_hw *, uint32_t, unsigned).
  n2ap_venc_start(enc, &p), set_param(enc, type, &p), encode(enc, in_handle, out_handle, N2AP_ENC_FRAME, &res), close(enc) all match; the FORCE_INTRA/SKIP_FRAME calls with NULL are explicitly accepted by V41 (n2ap_venc_set_param, cases at :952-955), so those are correct.
  The handles passed to encode are client DMA handles; V41 looks them up with n2vc_dma_lookup_handle and returns -EINVAL if the AP registry does not know them. vcodecds note_dma_handle() already reports that gap once per session ("needs RWVC_DMA_INFO"), which is exactly what happens: the missing piece is a way for the client/V40 to tell the AP process the PA of a client buffer (the RWVC_DMA_INFO request you proposed). That is a V40/V41 feature/interface addition, not a wrong call in vcodecd.
  I found no wrong argument, no guest pointer passed where a handle is expected, and no use of a V table that does not exist. If you add RWVC_DMA_INFO, V41s n2vc_dma_register_pa()/n2vc_dma_guest_register() are the two entry points to feed; n2vc_dma_lookup_handle() will then resolve the client handles.
For a full vcodecd review please ask hw-r2; my remit is V/T and I only checked the interface calls.
